newsitem.title: TURKEY: Hundreds demand prosecution of Turk Islamist MP.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds demand prosecution of Turk Islamist MP.

text.p: More than 400 people in an eastern Turkish city have demanded legal action against an Islamist firebrand MP for allegedly insulting them in a speech, Anatolian news agency said on Monday.
It said 422 residents of the city of Gaziantep had asked prosecutors in a written request to file a slander case against deputy Sevki Yilmaz.
Yilmaz resigned from the Islam-based Welfare Party last week after Turkish television showed an amateur video of him apparently accusing Gaziantep's mayor Celal Dogan of encouraging prostitution.

Anatolian said the residents also felt insulted because Dogan was their elected representative. "The petition...takes into acccount the rights of electors and those who voted for Dogan," the agency said.
Secularists were outraged by a series of video tapes, most of them several years old, which purported to show Yilmaz insulting mainstream politicians.
Yilmaz says the video tapes, shown recently on national television, may have been tampered with and his words changed.

Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, the head of Welfare, resigned last week under pressure from the country's powerful military over alleged activism. Yilmaz's speeches were held up by Turkey's secular media as examples of extremism.
